To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a joint training approach that unifies generative and contrastiv e objectives to improve the pre-training of language models for commonsense reasoning, which we evaluate on a variety of commonsense reasoning tasks.

(1) generative pre-training with the concept-centric common sense objective can improve the performance of PTLMs in a range of downstream NLU/NLG tasks that require commonsense knowledge, and (2) contrastive pre-training with a common sense objective is effective for downstream tasks that require commonsence reasoning, but it does not improve the performance of downstream tasks that require general language understanding.

(i) generative and contrastiv objectives are effective in improving the common sense of pre-trained language models; (ii) generative objectives are more effective than contrastive objectives in improving common sense; (iii) generative and con- trastive objectives can be effectively combined to improve common sense; (iv) the joint training framework is more effective than training each objective independently.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of: How can we improve PTLMs for downstream tasks that require commonsense reasoning?
the following questions: 1. How do we augment PTLMs for common sense pre-training?
the question: How to pre-train PTLMs with commonsense knowledge?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework is able to improve performance on downstream commonsense reasoning tasks.
we propose a new pre-training objective to improve the common sense of PTLMs, which is crucial for downstream commonsense reasoning tasks.
the proposed approach can be applied to any PTLM, such as T5 and BART, and that it can be used to improve the quality of commonsense knowledge in PTLMs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a joint training method to unify generative pre-training and contrastive pre-training for concept-centric commonsense.

we propose two new intermediate self-supervised tasks, generative task and contrastive task, to pre-train text-to-text Transformer models, and a new joint training framework to better leverage the two tasks.
we introduce a concept-centric pre-training objective to enhance PTLMs with commonsense knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pre-training PTLMs with concept-centric commonsense knowledge is an effective approach to improving their commonsense reasoning capabilities.

generative objectives are more effective than contrastive objectives in improving PTLMs' commonsense knowledge, and that the proposed joint training framework is more effective than training generative and contrastative objectives separately.
pre-trained language models augmented with common sense can achieve better performance on downstream tasks requiring common sense reasoning.
